questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

I know the most easiest way to solve this problem.
questions.solution: The correct answer is '**most easiest**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The **second segment** is erroneous. • The word '**easiest**' is the **superlative degree** of the adjective '**easy**'. • So, '**most**' should not be used with this word. • Hence, **option 2)** is the correct answer. **Correct sentence**__:* I know the easiest way to solve this problem.* * [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** * __ • **दूसरा खंड** गलत है। • '**easiest**' शब्द विशेषण '**easy**' का अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण अंश है। • अतः इस शब्द के साथ **'most'** का प्रयोग नहीं करना चाहिए। • अत: **option 2)** सही उत्तर है। [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • An **adjective** modifies a noun or a pronoun. • **Example__**: *Testbook is an amazing online learning platform*. • **Adjectives** have **three** different **forms of degrees** to show comparison: **positive degree**, **comparative degree**, **superlative degree**. • **Positive degree**: Positive degree is used to describe a **noun** and when there is no comparison. __ • **Example__**: *Lily is a good girl*. • **Comparative degree**: Comparative degree is used when two things or persons or objects are__ compared with each other.__ __ • **Example__**: *Lily is taller than Rahul*. • **Superlative degree**: Superlative degree is used when more than two persons or things or objects are compared. __ • **Example__**: *Lily is the tallest girl in the class*. 31:T67e, The correct answer is **he are good**

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

As a painter, he are good if not better than Suresh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **he are good**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how the subject of the sentence ('he') is as good as Suresh if in case he isn't better. 

 
• The subject **('he') is singular **in the sentence and so **all the verbs in the sentence need to follow this pattern. **
 
• For the verb form,** 'are' is the plural form.**
 
 
• *E.g. The people in the audience are getting bored.* 
 
 
 
• For the verb form, **'is' is the singular form.**
 
 
• *E.g. Rosa is really good at riding a motorcycle. *
 
 
 
• Thus, the** 'are' needs to be replaced with 'is'. **

Thus, the correct answer is **option 1. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, '**for**' should be used instead of '**since**'.
 
• ‘**For**’ refers to a specific period of time or a numerical value of time, for example for*** 2 years, for 4 weeks, for 3 hours, etc.***

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

Neither Mohit nor Rohit were there at the shop when I went there.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **were there**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Neither' and 'nor' are** correlative conjunctions** i.e., they are always used in **pair**.
 
• In case of **'neither…nor'**, always put **verb** according to the **subject** which is **closest**.
 
 
• For example: Neither my friends nor **I** **am** coming to meet you. (The verb 'am' is used as it is closest to the subject 'I')
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, the verb must agree with 'Rohit' (singular subject).
 
• Hence, 'was' (singular verb) must replace 'were' (plural verb).

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Neither Mohit nor Rohit** was** there at the shop when I went there.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Also, in case of **either…or**, always put the **verb** according to the **subject **which is **closest.**

 
 
• For example: Either my friends or **I am** coming to meet you. (In this sentence, the verb “am” agrees with the subject “I” because it is closest to it.)

questions.question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

The food / in the new eatery / is much best than / the one in RK Puram.
questions.solution: The correct answer is **'is much best than****.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The error lies in part **'is much best than'** of the sentence. • **Comparative adjectives** are used to compare differences between the two objects they modify (larger, smaller, faster, higher). • They are used in sentences where two nouns are compared, in this pattern: • **Noun (subject) + verb + much + comparative adjective + than + noun (object)**. • **Example**: *The rock flew **much higher than** the roof.* • Therefore, the use of **'much best than'** in the sentence should be replaced by 'much better than' to make it grammatically correct. • Therefore, the correct answer is 'is much best than.' • ​Correct sentence__: *The food in the new eatery **is much better than** the one in RK Puram.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** __ • When two items/people are compared, a comparative degree is used by putting ‘er’ to the adjective word in association with the word ‘than’. • In some cases ‘more’ is used. • Example: *She is smarter than her sister. She is more cheerful than her sister.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** • त्रुटि part 'is much best than' में निहित है।​ • Comparative adjectives उन दो वस्तुओं के बीच अंतर की तुलना करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है जिन्हें वे संशोधित करते हैं (बड़ा, छोटा, तेज, उच्च)। • उनका उपयोग उन वाक्यों में किया जाता है जहाँ दो संज्ञाओं की तुलना इस पैटर्न में की जाती है: • Noun (subject) + verb + much + comparative adjective + than + noun (object). • Example: *The rock flew much higher than the roof.* 34:T662, The erroneous segment is "**isn't it**"

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She / did not watched / Frankenstein / last night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect form of the verb **"watched"** in the phrase "**did not watched**."
 
• When using the auxiliary verb **"did,"** the main verb should be in** its base form.**
 
• The correct phrase should be "**did not watch**," ensuring grammatical correctness.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She **did not watch **Frankenstein last night."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "last night."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "She"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "Frankenstein"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The old man did not wanted to eat any food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3, i.e., did not wanted.**

Whenever a sentence uses the verb form '**did**', the corresponding verb must not use the past tense form of the verb.

As '**did**' already represents the past tense, using past tense form of the verb, viz, here, '**wanted**', is redundant.

So, the corrected sentence is: The old man **did not want** to eat any food.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.**

We ordered a Pizza / which are one of / my favourite foods.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'which are one of'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'which is one of' **should be used instead of **'which are one of'.**
 
• According to the **“Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”,** a **singular subject** always takes a **singular verb** and a** plural subject** always takes **a plural verb.**
 
• In the given sentence, ‘**Pizza**’ is **a singular subject** that will take ‘**is**’ as **a singular verb.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *We ordered a Pizza **which is one of** my favorite foods.*

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Rose painted the most beautifulest picture ever at the art class today!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the use of the double superlative "**most beautifulest**."
 
• Superlatives are used to indicate the highest degree of a quality, and typically, only one form (either "most" + adjective or adjective + "-est") should be used.
 
• The correct phrasing would be either "**the most beautiful**" or, less commonly for longer adjectives, "**the beautifulest**" (though the former is preferred).
 
• Therefore, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Rose painted **the most beautiful** picture ever at the art class today!"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) Rose painted** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• **2) picture ever at the** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• **4) art class today!** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• Using double superlatives like "most beautifulest" is a common grammatical mistake. It's important to use either the "most + adjective" form or the "adjective + -est" form, but not both together.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Pritha will been cooking / the meal of your choice / before you / reach home.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2: Pritha will been cooking".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment** "Pritha will been cooking"** contains a grammatical error.
 
• The correct form of future perfect continuous tense is **"Subject + will have been + verb-ing".** 
 
• Therefore, *"Pritha will been cooking" *should be **corrected to** *"Pritha will have been cooking"*.
 
• Furthermore, we use the future perfect continuous tense for actions that will be ongoing until a certain point in the future. This fits the given sentence context.
 
• Lastly, the other segments are grammatically correct and meaningful in the sentence context.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is **"Pritha will have been cooking".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1:** "reach home"** This segment is grammatically correct in this sentence context.
 
• Option 3: **"the meal of your choice" **This segment is grammatically accurate as it properly describes the meal.
 
• Option 4:** "before you"** This segment is accurate and serves to set the time reference for the future perfect continuous tense.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

The five first girls will get the discount on our merchandise.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3' **i.e.** 'The five first girls'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **error is in option 3) **"The five first girls."
 
• The **correct phrase** should be "The first five girls."
 
• In English, when describing a specific group of people or objects in a particular order, the **ordinal numbers** (such as "first," "second," "third") typically** come before **the **cardinal numbers** (such as "five," "ten," "twenty").
 
• Therefore, the **correct order** is "first five" instead of "five first."

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "**The first five girls **will get the discount on our merchandise."*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

He always / aimed highly / in life.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **aimed highly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace "**highly**" with "**high**" to correct the sentence.
 
• **Highly **is an adverb, which means at or to a high degree or level.
 
• We usually use '**highly**' as an intensifier to mean **'very, extremely, very much'.**
 
 
• Example - This is **highly **desirable.
 
 
 
• An **adverb **is a word that describes or modifies verbs, adjectives, clauses, and other adverbs. We use it to give additional information about other words.
 
• **High **can be used both as an adjective and as an adverb.
 
• It means** an elevated position or elevated condition.**
 
 
• **Example - **He threw the ball **high **into the sky.
 
 
 
• Here, in the given sentence, the more appropriate adverb is '**high**'.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: He had high standards for himself.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**, which contains an error in it.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *He always aimed **high__** in life.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

Each team were wearing a different coloured dress.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'Each team were'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'Each team was' **should be used instead of** 'Each team were'.**
 
• We know that after 'each, every, everyone, someone, nobody, one' a singular verb, singular noun, singular adjective, and a singular pronoun is used.
 
 
• *Example: Each student has come.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Each team was wearing a different coloured dress.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
